questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring a new academic setting while exdperiencing living in a foreign country. The fact that I could be close to friends and family in the country was a bonus; while making new connections and friendships and bonding over a shared experience. A different take on academia was also what I was craving and the other classes offered at the location.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the university had a good setup with informing the incoming students of events happening. The only complaint I have is that a lot of the introduction events were very generalised, targeted towards undergraduates or targeted to specific whole degrees at the university; none of which were relevant for me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None specifically, I just participated in the planned stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I do not remember all the options, I went with BY.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Again, since the opportunities were presented 6 months ago I do not remember any except where I ended up living. At BY there was communical kitchens.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is the best option if you are looking to make friends and meet a lot of people - I heard from other people living off campus that they had a hard time making friends and getting around while living off campus.

questions.answer: I do not remember it - it was 6 months ago.

questions.answer: On what scale? I got every class I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 500 courses, which are masters levels courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. I've learned that in DK we have much more training in oral presentation, while that is not prioritied much in other countries. At JCU there was a bigger focus on many small assignments throughout the teaching period and less on the final exam - and most of the exams were without aids at JCU as opposed to in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Soil properties and processes
Environmental Law and policy
Hazards and disasters
Advanced water resource system planning and management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what they are interested in. I loved the water class because it is an engineering class and I got to work closely with the professor and the engineering students and got a community through that class - but I could say the same about the hazards class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Well the public transportation system is very cheap but not very reliable or safe (I was told by people on campus to not take the bus alone at night), so I ended up renting a car, which is quite expensive - but the cost in ubers and taxis before that was running up as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Bus was very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None free, like at UCPH. But plenty of marine focused clubs, zoology club, scuba diving club, yoga club, a gym, a student bar etc. It was through my student housing that I got most of my cultural and athletic activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Yoga club and living on campus as most of the activities are "college v college" where one can only participate if they live on one of the campus collages.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Maggie island, get a car and drive up to the big and little crystal creek and visit the nearby towns and beaches.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy I'd say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really - language maybe? It gets fatigueing to talk to people of many different accents and understanding it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the indiginous culture bits.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the weather to be different than expected - it is a tropical destination, and I experienced both a flooding, a typhoon and an earthquake. 
Things work different there compared to DK, everything is slower and less developed. 
You might want to book your ticket to leave the day after finals ends and be out of there, but give yourself a few days after to soak the last of the experience up.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not particularly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning how the university wanted assignments to be written - very different from UCPH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
